title: CTGAN-augmented model predicts Kawasaki disease in a second-hospital validation cohort
summary: The authors developed stacked disease-classifier models, including a CTGAN-augmented version, using clinical data from febrile children. In validation at a second Taiwanese hospital, CTGAN-DC reported 95% sensitivity and 95% specificity for Kawasaki disease; the comparator model cited from prior work performed poorly on that cohort. This retrospective cross-hospital assessment is a model validation within the study, not prospective clinical testing or proof of improved care.
ai_technology: Stacked disease classifier with conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN) data augmentation

evidence.tested: The study evaluated the CTGAN-DC model using a second-hospital validation cohort and reported 95% sensitivity and specificity there.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation is retrospective and does not establish prospective clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; comparator differences should not be interpreted as independent replication.
evidence.ai_role: CTGAN augmentation and a stacked disease classifier were used to address class imbalance and predict Kawasaki disease among febrile children.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
